turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - cdft_piezo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose
    properties are NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal chemistry,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select the 5
candidates with the LARGEST piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij| (in
pC/N) that also satisfy a low-leakage requirement: the band gap must be at
least 5 eV. Band gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you must infer them. A
selected candidate whose band gap is below the threshold scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The piezoelectric strain tensor vanishes by symmetry in any centrosymmetric crystal, so the pool was first reduced to structures whose POSCAR coordinates are incompatible with inversion (odd-count sites that cannot sit on inversion centers, polar space-group types such as wurtzite-derived Pna2_{1} or Pmn2_{1}, or explicit polar displacements from a perovskite aristotype).

Among the surviving compounds the band-gap constraint \(E_g\ge5\,\mathrm{eV}\) was imposed from crystal chemistry: only highly ionic, closed-shell combinations of light main-group cations with O, F or Cl (no open d-shells, no stereochemically active lone pairs, no heavy chalcogenides or pnictides) were retained. This leaves a short list of phosphates, silicates, oxide wurtzites, fluoride frameworks and the chloride perovskite KCaCl_{3}.

Relative magnitudes of \(\max|d_{ij}|\) were then ranked by the usual structure–property rules:
- a weakly distorted polar perovskite (KCaCl_{3}) lies closest to a ferroelectric instability, producing a large dielectric susceptibility and therefore the highest \(d_{ij}\);
- polar wurtzite superstructures (NaGaO_{2}, Li_{2}ZnGeO_{4}) give the next-largest responses (typical \(d_{33}\sim5{-}15\,\mathrm{pC/N}\));
- three-dimensional phosphate and melilite networks remain piezoelectric but are stiffer and less polar, yielding smaller coefficients.

The five candidates that simultaneously maximize \(\max|d_{ij}|\) and satisfy the gap threshold are therefore

Final: c011, c018, c024, c005, c038
